new_statements.translation: 5.1.4. Stress. Stress in Yevanic, as in Standard Modern Greek (SMG), is dynamic. The trisyllabic rule [three-syllable window] is observed (in our data the development of a secondary stress, which Bongas 1964 observes for the Epirote dialects, has not been observed). The position of the stress is determined by the same rules that determine it in SMG (see Revithiadou 1999).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Dynamic (stress) accent identical to Standard Modern Greek: lexically/morphologically determined primary stress that must fall on one of the last three syllables of the word (antepenult, penult or final), with the SMG accent rules (Revithiadou 1999's lexical-accent analysis) applying unchanged.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Authors explicitly state that no secondary (rhythmic) stress was observed in their Yevanic data, unlike what Bongas 1964 reports for the surrounding Epirote dialects.
new_statements.exceptions: None; syllable structure (5.1.3) and stress (5.1.4) are said to show no observed differences from SMG. Segmental differences (unstressed e/o raising, unstressed i/u deletion, s-palatalization) are Ioannina/northern-dialect features that presuppose the same stress positions.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement based on field recordings (2013-2014) of elderly speakers in Ioannina and New York (Romaniote emigrants); ΚΝΕ = Κοινή Νέα Ελληνική (Standard Modern Greek).
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes present-day Yevanic/Romaniote Judeo-Greek (γεβανική, ρωμανιώτικα, καστρινά) as spoken by elderly Romaniote Jews of Ioannina and Ioannina-origin emigrants in New York (fieldwork 2013-2014); the authors treat it as a variety of Greek heavily shaped by the Ioannina (Epirote, semi-northern) dialect. Matches Glottolog yeva1238 / ISO yej; no separate dialect glottocode involved.

sources.note: Dedicated section 5.1.4 'Τονισμός' (p. 49): stress is dynamic as in Standard Modern Greek; the three-syllable window rule holds; stress position is determined by the same rules as in SMG (ref. Revithiadou 1999); no secondary stress observed in their data (contra Bongas 1964 for Epirote dialects). Section 5.1.3: syllable structure identical to SMG. 5.1.2 documents unstressed mid-vowel raising and unstressed high-vowel deletion (northern vocalism).

sources.note: Section 3.1 Phonology (pp. 55-56): 'the sound system of Yevanic differs minimally from that of SMG'; lists postalveolars, unstressed [e o] raising and unstressed [i u] deletion, Ioannina-dialect processes.
